display.title: Parshas Toldos: Turning the Yetzer Hara's Tricks Around (Alternate Take)
display.summary_short: Another recording of the Toldos lesson: Rivkah's twins, the two inclinations, and a hotel keeper saved in court by the very condition that made him liable.
display.summary_long: This week's parsha begins with Rivkah, troubled when the baby seemed to push toward both a yeshiva and a place of idol worship, and calmed once she learned she was carrying twins, Yaakov and Esav. The Alter Rebbe learns from this that a person has two separate souls, a good and an evil inclination, so stray thoughts during davening do not mean the davening is worthless; the yetzer hara comes precisely because the davening is good. Hashem gave us a yetzer hara so we grow stronger by overcoming it, and we can even turn its suggestions around: steal time from play for learning. The story: three businessmen leave their money with a hotel keeper on condition he return it only to all three. One tricks him and runs off with it, and the court makes the hotel keeper pay. His Rav argues that he will pay, but only to all three together, so the condition that condemned him saves him. The storyteller adds Rabbi Zusha's seven lessons from a thief, the Shema's "levavcha", a boy who stole coins being made the tzedakah treasurer, and the Rebbe's advice to make an energetic child a leader.
display.lesson: The yetzer hara is there to make us stronger; we can use its own tricks and our own energies to serve Hashem better.

characters: the businessmen Chaim, Yankel and Shmerel
